name: Incisionless Fritsch otoplasty
lead: Incisionless (percutaneous) otoplasty, associated with Fritsch, places sutures through the skin with needles to shape the antihelix and conchal bowl, without a skin incision. Wikipedia dates Fritsch's publications on the method from 1995 to 2009 and notes it may be combined with superficial scoring of the cartilage.[1]

Grokipedia describes incisionless suturing generally as suited to mild to moderate prominent ears, without naming a technique.[2] No clinical studies were found for this specific method in the sources reviewed.

paras: Per Wikipedia, needle-placed sutures through the skin shape the antihelix and concha, sometimes with superficial scoring.[1] Grokipedia says incisionless approaches suit mild to moderate prominence.[2]

card.summary: Ear pinning with needle-placed stitches through the skin and no incision; documented, but outcome data are thin.
card.note: Described as suited to milder cases; few outcome data located.

quick.overview:
Incisionless otoplasty reshapes the ear using sutures passed through the skin by needle, avoiding a cut behind the ear. Fritsch published on it between 1995 and 2009.

Sources are brief.
quick.mechanism: Percutaneous sutures fold the antihelix and set back the concha, sometimes with scoring.
quick.risks: No technique-specific studies were found; general otoplasty risks apply, and sources describe it as suited to mild to moderate prominence.
